name: Cat First Aid Checklist
description: A cat-specific checklist to help owners respond to wounds, possible poisoning, and breathing trouble and know when to call the vet.

items.text: Save your vet and nearest emergency hospital numbers
Keep a pet poison helpline number handy
Stock and check a cat first aid kit
Learn your cat's normal breathing and gum color
Keep a carrier and towel within easy reach
items.note: Program emergency numbers into your phone in advance

items.text: Move slowly and speak in a soft, calm voice
Wrap a frightened cat gently in a towel if needed
Support the body and avoid sudden movements
Watch for signs of fear, pain, or aggression
Protect yourself from bites and scratches
items.note: An injured cat may lash out even if usually gentle

items.text: Apply gentle, steady pressure with a clean cloth
Hold pressure rather than checking repeatedly
Keep your cat calm and limit movement
Note bite wounds, which can hide deep damage
See a vet for deep, dirty, or heavy bleeding
items.note: Heavy or spurting bleeding is an emergency, so go at once

items.text: Note the substance and amount; keep the packaging
Do not induce vomiting unless a vet directs it
Keep your cat away from the source
Watch for drooling, tremors, or vomiting
Call a vet or poison helpline immediately
items.note: Many plants and household items are toxic to cats

items.text: Look for open-mouth or rapid, labored breathing
Check gums for a blue or pale color
Keep your cat as calm and still as possible
Avoid stressing or restraining too firmly
Rush to emergency care without delay
Place your cat gently in a secure carrier
Support an injured body and avoid twisting
Keep the carrier warm, dark, and quiet
Call ahead so the clinic can prepare
Bring any packaging, medicines, or samples
This checklist is general information for owners, not veterinary advice; first aid does not replace professional care, so always consult a licensed veterinarian
items.note: In any emergency, contact your vet or an emergency animal hospital immediately

faq.q: How do I treat a cat's wound at first?
faq.a: Apply gentle, steady pressure with a clean cloth to stop bleeding and keep your cat calm. Even small bite wounds can become infected, so have a vet examine wounds rather than relying on home care alone.

faq.q: What are signs my cat may be poisoned?
faq.a: Watch for drooling, vomiting, tremors, unsteadiness, breathing trouble, or sudden lethargy. Note what they may have contacted, keep any packaging, and call a vet or pet poison helpline immediately for guidance.

faq.q: How can I tell if my cat is having trouble breathing?
faq.a: Signs include open-mouth or rapid breathing, sides heaving, blue or pale gums, or hiding while struggling. Breathing trouble is an emergency, so keep your cat calm and get to a vet right away.

faq.q: Why do cats hide when they are sick or hurt?
faq.a: Hiding is a natural instinct that can mask pain or illness. If your cat suddenly hides, stops eating, or changes behavior, treat it seriously and contact your veterinarian to be safe.

faq.q: Is this cat first aid checklist printable?
faq.a: Yes. Print it or download the PDF, keep it with your cat's emergency kit, and review it so the steps are familiar before you need them.
